beats.say: Criminal case, court summons, tax debt. Words like these frighten people, and scammers count on that.
Such emails also reach state institution addresses. The attachment often hides malware.

body.text: Your name appears in a criminal case. The materials are attached.

beats.say: Others demand an immediate payment for a debt or fine, through a link.

messages.text: Your tax debt is 186.40 AZN. Pay today:

beats.say: Check the notice yourself, using the number on the agency's official website or its official portal.

scenes.prompt: Find the signs of fraud in this notice.

body.text: you are named as a suspect in a criminal case.
If you do not reply within 24 hours, an arrest order will be issued.
Open the attachment to read the case materials.
Do not tell anyone about this email.

spots.label: Fake domain
spots.explain: The domain looks official but is not. Open the agency's website yourself and compare.

spots.label: Generic greeting
spots.explain: A real notice addressed to you carries your name, not "dear citizen".

spots.label: Arrest threat and 24 hours
spots.explain: Fear and a short deadline push you to act without thinking.

spots.label: Do not tell anyone
spots.explain: They want to cut you off from help. Instead, tell the security team at once.

spots.label: Archive file
spots.explain: An archive can carry malware. Do not open an archive you did not expect.

scenes.title: Frightening mail
scenes.intro: Your mailbox has four emails in the name of official bodies. Check each one and decide.

body.text: Your name appears in a criminal case. Read the attached materials within 24 hours.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. Fake domain, threat and archive: reporting protects your colleagues too.

actions.label: Open attachment
actions.feedback: The file in the archive launched malware. Disconnect the computer from the network and report it at once.

actions.label: Reply
actions.feedback: A reply tells the scammer your address is live. More threats will follow.

body.text: You must appear in court tomorrow at 10:00.

actions.label: Download summons
actions.feedback: The link downloaded a malicious file. The summons should have been checked using the court's official number.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. Report a summons from a foreign domain and call the court yourself if needed.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Safe. But if you report it, your colleagues are protected too.

body.text: If you do not pay today, your bank accounts will be frozen.

actions.label: Pay online
actions.feedback: The fake payment page took your card details. Call your bank now and block the card.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right. Check any debt only by signing in to the official portal yourself.

body.text: This week staff are receiving fake "criminal case" emails. Do not open attachments, report such emails as phishing.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. A warning from your own legal department, with no link or attachment.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Not every email is a threat. This is a useful warning from your own institution.

question.prompt: The email says the case will be closed if you pay half the fine today.

options.label: I pay so it does not get worse
options.feedback: Official bodies do not "close" cases for a payment by link. The money goes straight to the scammer.

options.label: I call the number in the email to ask
options.feedback: That number belongs to the scammer. They will only frighten you more.

options.label: I find the agency's number on its official website and call
options.feedback: Right. When you find the contact yourself, a fake notice is exposed at once.

scenes.explain: Threats, urgency and a payment demand together mean fraud. Report the email to the security team as well.

scenes.prompt: Match each trick with its purpose.

pairs.left: Threat of arrest or a criminal case
pairs.right: Use fear to leave no time to think
Keep you from asking for advice

scenes.explain: However serious the threat sounds, the steps are the same: stop, check through an official channel, report.

points: Threats, urgency and payment demands are signs of a fake notice.
Do not open unexpected attachments or links, report the email as phishing.
Check a notice yourself using the number on the agency's official website.
